evaluator_note: All complete responses individually read and checked against each requested part. Incidental expected-answer details not requested by question are not silently added to rubric. Equivalent wording accepted; no borrowing between answers.

grades.question: How are the King and home regions assigned, and where do each player’s initial ten Caballeros go?
grades.expected_answer: Shuffle region cards; reveal top for King, each player takes another for home and places Grande. Two Caballeros home, one on first success-track space, seven court; remaining supply provinces.

observed.answer: Shuffle the nine region cards; reveal the top card and place the King there. Each player takes another card for their home region and places their Grande there. Each starts with ten Caballeros: two beside the Grande in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in their court.
observed.evidence: Setup: “two in their home region beside the Grande, one on the first space ... and seven in their court.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Shuffle region cards; reveal top for King, each player takes another for home and places Grande. Two Caballeros home, one on first success-track space, seven court; remaining supply provinces.

grades.question: Who begins playing power cards in the first and later rounds, in what seating direction do others play, and may a played value be matched?
grades.expected_answer: Players choose first-round starter; previous round’s last player begins later rounds; clockwise; no duplicate value in a round.

observed.answer: In round 1, the players choose who starts. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round starts. Others play clockwise, and no power-card value already played that round may be matched.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “later, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins”; “Others play clockwise”; “No value already played this round may be matched.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Players choose first-round starter; previous round’s last player begins later rounds; clockwise; no duplicate value in a round.

grades.question: What determines turn order and court recruitment, and when is recruitment done relative to choosing an action card?
grades.expected_answer: Descending power value determines turns. Recruit at most pictured Caballeros from provinces into court first, then choose face-up action card.

observed.answer: Players take turns in descending power-card value. At the start of a turn, recruit up to the number shown on that power card from the provinces into court; recruiting fewer is allowed. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “At the start of your turn recruit up to the number ... from the provinces into your court”; then “After recruitment, choose an available face-up action card.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Descending power value determines turns. Recruit at most pictured Caballeros from provinces into court first, then choose face-up action card.

grades.question: If a power card allows recruitment but your provinces lack enough, what alternative is allowed, and which protected locations cannot supply it?
grades.expected_answer: May remove own Caballeros from board to make up difference; not King’s region or Castillo (taboo and no Castillo removal outside general scoring).

observed.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King’s region is taboo, and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “you may take your own from the board to make up the difference”; “The King’s region remains taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: May remove own Caballeros from board to make up difference; not King’s region or Castillo (taboo and no Castillo removal outside general scoring).

grades.question: Where may ordinary action-card deployment go, may it be split, and must the full printed allowance be used?
grades.expected_answer: From court to regions adjacent to current King and/or Castillo; split freely; printed number is maximum, fewer allowed.

observed.answer: Ordinary deployment moves up to the action card’s number from your court to regions adjacent to the King’s current region and/or the Castillo, with the allowance dividable freely. It cannot be split into separate parts around another activity (see Q06), but can be divided among destinations. The printed allowance is a maximum; you may deploy fewer or none.
observed.evidence: Actions: “number is a maximum”; “may deploy fewer, including none”; “dividing the allowance freely.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: From court to regions adjacent to current King and/or Castillo; split freely; printed number is maximum, fewer allowed.

grades.question: May special action and ordinary deployment be done in either order, may either be interleaved with the other, and may the special action be declined?
grades.expected_answer: Either order, each completed wholly before next; no splitting/interleaving. Special action optional, may select card to prevent it.

observed.answer: Yes. Ordinary deployment and the special action may be done in either order, but each must be completed as a whole before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. You may decline the special action.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “Do them in either order ... neither may be split or interleaved”; “You may decline the special action.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Either order, each completed wholly before next; no splitting/interleaving. Special action optional, may select card to prevent it.

grades.question: What happens to selected and unselected face-up action cards after turns and rounds, and what is exceptional about the King card?
grades.expected_answer: Chosen card laid aside unavailable to later players; remaining face-up cards discarded at round end; King card returns face-up every round, never permanently discarded.

observed.answer: After a turn, lay the selected action card aside so later players cannot choose it. After everyone has taken a turn, discard remaining face-up action cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “Lay aside the selected action card”; “discard any remaining face-up action cards”; “King card ... never permanently discarded.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Chosen card laid aside unavailable to later players; remaining face-up cards discarded at round end; King card returns face-up every round, never permanently discarded.

grades.question: What changes are forbidden in the King’s region, may it still be scored, and what kind of action changes its protected status?
grades.expected_answer: No Caballeros, Grande or mobile scoreboard in/out, even special actions; scoring allowed. King-moving actions move King, changing which region is taboo.

observed.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King’s region; it may still be scored. Moving the King changes which region is protected.
observed.evidence: Protected locations: “no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it. ... It may still be scored. Actions that move the King are the exception.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: No Caballeros, Grande or mobile scoreboard in/out, even special actions; scoring allowed. King-moving actions move King, changing which region is taboo.

grades.question: When putting Caballeros into the Castillo, what must be announced, how does King location affect entry, and when may they leave?
grades.expected_answer: Announce number added; entry whenever adding/moving Caballeros regardless King; leave only at general scoring.

observed.answer: Clearly announce how many Caballeros you put in the Castillo. They may enter regardless of the King’s location. They may leave only during general scoring; no action removes them.
observed.evidence: Actions: “Announce clearly how many you put inside”; “regardless of the King’s location”; “leave only during general scoring.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Announce number added; entry whenever adding/moving Caballeros regardless King; leave only at general scoring.

grades.question: List the timing and ordered stages of general scoring, including when destinations are chosen relative to revealing the Castillo.
grades.expected_answer: After rounds 3,6,9: secretly choose destinations first and place disks face down; uncover and score Castillo; reveal disks and move its Caballeros; score board regions in track order.

observed.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: (1) each player secretly chooses one destination region for all their Castillo Caballeros, setting a face-down disk before the Castillo is uncovered; (2) uncover and score the Castillo; (3) reveal disks and move all Castillo Caballeros to the chosen regions, then replace the empty Castillo; (4) score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
observed.evidence: General scoring: “Secretly select destinations before uncovering the Castillo”; then score Castillo, reveal disks/empty Castillo, and score nine regions. Overview gives rounds 3, 6 and 9.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: After rounds 3,6,9: secretly choose destinations first and place disks face down; uncover and score Castillo; reveal disks and move its Caballeros; score board regions in track order.

grades.question: At general scoring, may one player split Castillo Caballeros between regions, choose the King’s region, or keep them in the Castillo; what happens if the King’s region was chosen?
grades.expected_answer: All must go to single disk-selected region, not King’s region; Castillo emptied. Illegal King choice sends own Castillo Caballeros to own court.

observed.answer: A player must send all their Castillo Caballeros to one region, not split them. The King’s region is prohibited as a destination, and no pieces may be kept in the Castillo after its general scoring. If a player illegally chose the King’s region, their pieces go to their court; that consequence does not make the choice permitted.
observed.evidence: General scoring: “All that player’s Castillo Caballeros must go to one region”; “Choosing the King’s region is prohibited”; illegal choice sends pieces to court; Castillo is replaced empty.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: All must go to single disk-selected region, not King’s region; Castillo emptied. Illegal King choice sends own Castillo Caballeros to own court.

grades.question: In a four-player scoring of 5/3/1, three players have four Caballeros each and another has three. What do these four players score, and do Grandes count?
grades.expected_answer: Three tied leaders each 3 (second rank); next player third rank gets1. Grandes do not count toward majority.

observed.answer: The three players tied at four each receive second-place value, 3 points each; the player with three receives third-place value, 1 point. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
observed.evidence: Example: “4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1”; “Only Caballeros count toward majority. A Grande ... contributes zero Caballeros.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Three tied leaders each 3 (second rank); next player third rank gets1. Grandes do not count toward majority.

grades.question: In a four-player region worth 6/4/2 with counts 4,3,2,2, what scoreboard points does each player receive before any King’s or home-region bonuses?
grades.expected_answer: 6,4,0,0 scoreboard points: the two players tied for third drop to fourth and receive no scoreboard points. This question asks only for points from the scoreboard, before bonuses.

observed.answer: The player with four receives 6 points; the player with three receives 4; each player with two receives 0.
observed.evidence: Publisher scoring example: “On 6/4/2, counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: 6,4,0,0 scoreboard points: the two players tied for third drop to fourth and receive no scoreboard points. This question asks only for points from the scoreboard, before bonuses.

grades.question: Which scoreboard ranks pay in two-player and three-player games, and what happens to a two-player tie for first?
grades.expected_answer: Two players only first rank; three only first two. Tied first drops to second so two-player tied leaders receive no points.

observed.answer: In a two-player game only first place can pay; in a three-player game first and second can pay. A tie for first shifts to second-place value, but the two-player cutoff then means neither player scores.
observed.evidence: Region ranks: “Two players: only first place can pay. Three players: only first and second can pay”; “a two-player tie for first pays neither player.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Two players only first rank; three only first two. Tied first drops to second so two-player tied leaders receive no points.

grades.question: When are the King’s and home bonuses awarded, how much is each, and what happens on a tied majority?
grades.expected_answer: Whenever relevant region scored including special scoring; sole majority earns2 King bonus in King region and2 home bonus if own Grande there; neither for tied first.

observed.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scoring, the sole majority holder in the King’s region gets +2, and the sole majority holder with their own Grande in a region gets +2. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
observed.evidence: Bonuses: apply “whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scorings”; each is +2; “Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Whenever relevant region scored including special scoring; sole majority earns2 King bonus in King region and2 home bonus if own Grande there; neither for tied first.

grades.question: Does specially scoring the Castillo empty it or redistribute its Caballeros? Describe what happens.
grades.expected_answer: Uncover and score; replace Castillo over same Caballeros; no redistribution until general scoring.

observed.answer: Specially scoring the Castillo reveals and scores its pieces, then covers those same pieces again. It does not empty or redistribute them; they leave only at general scoring.
observed.evidence: Actions: “Special scoring of the Castillo reveals and scores its contents, then covers them again without redistribution.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Uncover and score; replace Castillo over same Caballeros; no redistribution until general scoring.

grades.question: Can a mobile scoreboard be put at the Castillo, moved into/out of King’s region, stacked on the other, or rotated to change its values?
grades.expected_answer: Castillo allowed; King in/out prohibited; cannot stack; right side up only8/4/0 or4/0/0.

observed.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King’s region, the two scoreboards may not be stacked, and they may not be reversed or rotated to change their values.
observed.evidence: Stack 4: Castillo allowed; “No movement into or out of the King’s region”; “cannot be stacked”; place right side up, never reversed or rotated.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Castillo allowed; King in/out prohibited; cannot stack; right side up only8/4/0 or4/0/0.

grades.question: What are the legal source/destination restrictions on moving your Grande, may other Grandes already be there, and what changes afterward?
grades.expected_answer: Cannot leave King region or enter King region/Castillo; any other region even multiple Grandes; new region is home.

observed.answer: You may move your Grande to another region except the King’s region or Castillo; a Grande in the King’s region cannot leave. The destination may already contain several Grandes. The destination becomes your new home region.
observed.evidence: Stack 4—Grande: “another region except the King’s region or Castillo”; destination may already contain several Grandes; “destination becomes your new home region.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Cannot leave King region or enter King region/Castillo; any other region even multiple Grandes; new region is home.

grades.question: Which power card may the recovery action return, can it be the card used this turn, and must the choice be revealed?
grades.expected_answer: Any one played card, including current turn’s, to hand; need not reveal, though taking visible top is observable.

observed.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the one played this turn. You need not reveal which card you choose, although taking the visible top card is apparent.
observed.evidence: Stack 4—Power Cards: “any one ... including the one played this turn”; “You need not reveal which.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Any one played card, including current turn’s, to hand; need not reveal, though taking visible top is observable.

grades.question: When does the standard game end, and how is the winner determined?
grades.expected_answer: After third general scoring following round9; furthest along success track/most points wins.

observed.answer: The game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins.
observed.evidence: End: “Finish all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9”; furthest along the success track wins.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: After third general scoring following round9; furthest along success track/most points wins.

grades.question: How are action stacks prepared, how many cards are revealed at the start of each round, and where does the standard round marker start?
grades.expected_answer: Separate stacks by backs1–5, shuffle each separately face down (eleven each in1–4, sole King in5). Reveal top of each, five total. Marker starts space1; advance one each later round.

observed.answer: Separate the action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place them face down beside the board. At the start of each round, reveal the top card of each of the five stacks (five choices). The standard round marker starts at 1.
observed.evidence: Setup: stack by 1–5, shuffle separately; round marker at 1. Turn Structure: reveal top card of each of five action stacks.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Separate stacks by backs1–5, shuffle each separately face down (eleven each in1–4, sole King in5). Reveal top of each, five total. Marker starts space1; advance one each later round.

grades.question: After you play a power card, is it returned to hand for later rounds, and how are played cards displayed?
grades.expected_answer: No, stays face up in own used stack with only top card visible; recovery special action required to retrieve one.

observed.answer: A played power card is not returned to hand; it remains in that player’s face-up used stack, with only the top card visible. A special action can recover a played card.
observed.evidence: Turn Structure: “Played cards remain in each player’s face-up used stack with only the top card visible”; special action can recover one.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: No, stays face up in own used stack with only top card visible; recovery special action required to retrieve one.

grades.question: If you use the King card’s special action before deploying, which King position controls deployment, and where may the King be placed?
grades.expected_answer: Current new position governs adjacent destinations; special action may place King in any board region except Castillo. If deploy first, old position applies.

observed.answer: If the King card’s special action is done before ordinary deployment, the King’s new position determines the adjacent destinations. The King may be placed in any region except the Castillo.
observed.evidence: King card: put King in “any region except Castillo”; use current location at time of deployment. Protected locations: moving King first means use new position.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Current new position governs adjacent destinations; special action may place King in any board region except Castillo. If deploy first, old position applies.

grades.question: How is a Veto card retained, what can it prevent, and can it stop the ordinary deployment part of another action card?
grades.expected_answer: Place it before you and retain to prevent one special action; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

observed.answer: Keep the Veto card before you to retain it. It can stop one special action during this round or the next, but cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion of an action card.
observed.evidence: Stack 2—Veto: “Put the card before you and retain it”; stops one special action; “It cannot stop the ordinary deployment portion.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Place it before you and retain to prevent one special action; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

grades.question: With Veto held, must other players announce special actions, when should you object, and what happens if it is partly or fully completed?
grades.expected_answer: Others announce before executing. Object as soon as action begins, may veto announced action before execution; may stop only part/remainder while incomplete. Completed action cannot be vetoed.

observed.answer: While you hold Veto, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete special action. A completed action cannot be vetoed, and already executed parts are not undone; you may stop just part.
observed.evidence: Veto: players “must announce special actions before executing them”; object “as soon as the player starts”; completed actions cannot be vetoed and executed parts are not undone.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Others announce before executing. Object as soon as action begins, may veto announced action before execution; may stop only part/remainder while incomplete. Completed action cannot be vetoed.

grades.question: When is Veto discarded after use, and when does an unused Veto expire?
grades.expected_answer: After one veto discard immediately; unused discard at end of round following selection. Usable selection round or next.

observed.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
observed.evidence: Veto: “Discard after using the veto once; if unused, discard at the end of the next round.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: After one veto discard immediately; unused discard at end of round following selection. Usable selection round or next.

grades.question: Who is affected by the all-court Decay of Authority card and where do those Caballeros go, including a player with an empty court?
grades.expected_answer: Fellow players/opponents send all court Caballeros to provinces; actor excluded; empty court sends none.

observed.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A fellow player with an empty court sends none.
observed.evidence: Decay of Authority—all court: “Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces”; “an empty court sends none”; selecting player unaffected.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Fellow players/opponents send all court Caballeros to provinces; actor excluded; empty court sends none.

grades.question: For Decay of Authority requiring three from each fellow player’s court, what happens if a fellow player has two and you have five?
grades.expected_answer: Opponent sends both to provinces; each opponent with fewer3 sends all court. Actor sends none and retains five.

observed.answer: The fellow player with two sends both, since they send all they have if fewer than three. You are unaffected and keep your five.
observed.evidence: Decay of Authority—three from court: “three ... or all they have if fewer than three”; selecting player unaffected.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Opponent sends both to provinces; each opponent with fewer3 sends all court. Actor sends none and retains five.

grades.question: For The King returns!, what does the detailed execution paragraph require about participants, amount, sources and order, and how does its heading differ?
grades.expected_answer: Detailed paragraph says each player sends3 own Caballeros to provinces, starting actor’s left clockwise (thus actor last). Sources any regions and/or court except King’s region/Castillo. Heading says fellow players; detailed paragraph and card face say each player.

observed.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and matching card face require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Start with the player to the selecting player’s left, proceed clockwise, and have the selecting player go last. Each chooses their pieces from any regions and/or their court, but not the King’s region or Castillo. The summary says the source gives no explicit shortfall rule if a player has fewer than three eligible pieces. The bold heading instead says “fellow players.”
observed.evidence: Stack 2—The King returns: detailed paragraph/card says each player including selecting player sends three; stated order and source exclusions; heading says “fellow players.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Detailed paragraph says each player sends3 own Caballeros to provinces, starting actor’s left clockwise (thus actor last). Sources any regions and/or court except King’s region/Castillo. Heading says fellow players; detailed paragraph and card face say each player.

grades.question: On the action sending one Caballero from each player from any region back to provinces, who chooses the pieces, does the acting player lose one, and what sources are excluded?
grades.expected_answer: Actor chooses one from each player including own; region sources only, not King’s region or Castillo (not courts). Return provinces.

observed.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner’s provinces. Pieces cannot be taken from courts, the King’s region, or Castillo.
observed.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one “for each player, including themselves”; no taking from courts, King’s region, or Castillo.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Actor chooses one from each player including own; region sources only, not King’s region or Castillo (not courts). Return provinces.

grades.question: For the secret removal of two own Caballeros from a region, how do affected fellow players choose and reveal, and what region must a player with a legal region containing at least two choose?
grades.expected_answer: Simultaneous secret disk choices revealed together; each affected opponent chooses one region containing at least2 own, returns2 to provinces; cannot take from King region/Castillo.

observed.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects a region on their disk, with choices simultaneous and revealed together. A player who has at least one legal region containing two or more of their own Caballeros must choose a region containing at least two of their Caballeros. The King’s region and Castillo are excluded.
observed.evidence: Secretly remove two: simultaneous secret disk selection, reveal together; choose a region with at least two of that player’s Caballeros; never take from King’s region or Castillo.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Simultaneous secret disk choices revealed together; each affected opponent chooses one region containing at least2 own, returns2 to provinces; cannot take from King region/Castillo.

grades.question: For secret removal of two, if a fellow player has single own Caballeros in legal regions but never more than one in any region, what selection and removal is required?
grades.expected_answer: Select a region containing one own Caballero and return that one to provinces; cannot take from King region or Castillo.

observed.answer: If they have at most one in every region, the stated singleton fallback is to choose a region with one and return that one to the provinces.
observed.evidence: Secretly remove two: “The stated singleton fallback applies if the player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.”

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Select a region containing one own Caballero and return that one to provinces; cannot take from King region or Castillo.

grades.question: For fellow players secretly returning all their own Caballeros from one region, what must the chosen region contain, how is it selected, and what if a player has no Caballeros in any region?
grades.expected_answer: Simultaneous secret disks then reveal; selected legal region must contain at least1 own; return all own there to provinces; no board-region Caballeros means unaffected. King region/Castillo excluded.

observed.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses a region containing at least one of their Caballeros on a disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. They return all their own Caballeros there to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
observed.evidence: Secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous secret disk selection; choose a region with at least one; return all their own there; player with none is unaffected.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Simultaneous secret disks then reveal; selected legal region must contain at least1 own; return all own there to provinces; no board-region Caballeros means unaffected. King region/Castillo excluded.

grades.question: For the special action choosing any one location to score, may you choose the King’s region or Castillo, do ordinary scoring rules apply, and are Castillo pieces redistributed?
grades.expected_answer: Yes either; ordinary Score Regions rules including applicable bonuses/rank limits. Castillo scored then covered again, not redistributed.

observed.answer: Yes, choose any region, including the King’s region, or the Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score and cover the same pieces again; they are not redistributed.
observed.evidence: Pick one region: any region including King’s region or Castillo; normal rules and bonuses; Castillo pieces covered again without redistribution.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Yes either; ordinary Score Regions rules including applicable bonuses/rank limits. Castillo scored then covered again, not redistributed.

grades.question: For scoring all 4-value regions, name the printed group and explain what value determines eligibility when mobile scoreboards are present. Specifically, Galicia has8/4/0 and Granada4/0/0: which qualifies, and do bonuses apply?
grades.expected_answer: Printed group Galicia4/2/0, Catalonia4/2/1, Seville4/3/1. Use current mobile scoreboard first value instead of covered printed values; Galicia not4 excluded, Granada4 qualifies; normal home/King bonuses apply.

observed.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is determined by a region’s current first value, so Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify and Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scorings.
observed.evidence: Stack 3—all 4-value regions: current first value determines group; mobile example says 8/4/0 in Galicia removes it and 4/0/0 in Granada adds Granada. Bonuses apply to special scorings.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: Printed group Galicia4/2/0, Catalonia4/2/1, Seville4/3/1. Use current mobile scoreboard first value instead of covered printed values; Galicia not4 excluded, Granada4 qualifies; normal home/King bonuses apply.

grades.question: Which printed regions are the 5-value group and the 6-and-7-value group, how do mobile scoreboards affect these groups, and is the Castillo included in all-5 scoring?
grades.expected_answer: 5: Basque Country5/3/1, Aragon5/4/1, Valencia5/3/2. 6/7: Old Castile6/4/2, New Castile7/4/2, Granada6/3/1. Current mobile first value overrides printed category. Castillo not scored by all5.

observed.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country (5/3/1), Aragon (5/4/1), and Valencia (5/3/2). The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile (6/4/2), New Castile (7/4/2), and Granada (6/3/1). For both cards, current first value determines eligibility, so mobile scoreboards can remove a printed member or add another region. Castillo is explicitly not scored by the all-5 card.
observed.evidence: Stack 3 lists the printed groups and says current first value determines 5 or 6/7 eligibility; “Castillo is not scored” for all-5.

grades.reason: All requested material rulings correct and summary-supported. Fixed reference: 5: Basque Country5/3/1, Aragon5/4/1, Valencia5/3/2. 6/7: Old Castile6/4/2, New Castile7/4/2, Granada6/3/1. Current mobile first value overrides printed category. Castillo not scored by all5.

grades.question: When the first-position-only scoring card is used, what do tied leaders and lower ranks score, and is the Castillo scored?
